A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPDstergm research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across removals, restructuring, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SBM and STERGM simulations, MIT cellphone and stock-market change-point analyses, portfolio simulations, and fitted stock-network coefficients.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation results in Tables 1–6 and the MIT cellphone and stock-market change-point analyses in Sections 5.2–5.3.

M1.justification: The STERGM pseudo-likelihood objective, group fused lasso penalty, ADMM updates, thresholding, post-processing, and BIC selection remain unchanged. Added explanations clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The SBM and STERGM scenarios and MIT and stock-market detection tasks remain. V2 removes the auxiliary portfolio-construction task and subsequent stock-network parameter-estimation analysis, narrowing downstream task coverage within the retained financial domain.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate gSeg and kerSeg with network and network-statistic inputs in simulations. Their participation and input choices in the MIT and stock-market comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The removed analyses eliminate the 10-stock, 24-week portfolio protocol and three stock-network fits using 24-week windows. Retained simulation settings, evaluation metrics, optimization budgets, and real-data preprocessing are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the portfolio-behavior illustration around October 2008 and the analysis of formation and persistence coefficients across financial regimes. Existing comparisons across temporal dependence, network complexity, and input representations remain.

E5.justification: V2 removes the standard errors and 0.01-level significance markings accompanying the auxiliary coefficients in v1 Table 5, along with the portfolio experiment's 100-repeat reporting. Both versions retain the same ten-trial Monte Carlo means for detection benchmarks.

E6.justification: The portfolio-return findings in v1 Figure 1 and twelve stock-network coefficient estimates in v1 Table 5 disappear. All 90 simulation result rows match between v1 Tables 1–2 and v2 Tables 1–6; reported MIT and stock-market change points are unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A's minimum-variance portfolio objective, budget constraint, and closed-form weights are removed. The STERGM mathematics and Newton–Raphson and group-lasso derivations remain, with v1 Appendices B–C becoming v2 Appendices A–B.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about simultaneous detection using STERGM, ADMM and group fused lasso, BIC selection, nodal attributes, empirical performance, and the R package.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 newly specifies that the detector's parameter estimates are not intended for interpreting network effects. V2 also removes the portfolio-decision argument and coefficient-based interpretations of market volatility, momentum, and investor confidence. Existing baseline-comparison caveats and future-work limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 removes portfolio-calculation instructions, including short-sale allowance, and details of the separate stock-market STERGM fits and persistence parameterization. CPDstergm implementation settings, network-statistic definitions, and the code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Caimo and Gollini (2020) to the weighted-network discussion and removes Blackburn and Handcock (2022) and Elton et al. (2009). Kei et al.'s publication update refers to the same work. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 trims the introduction and financial discussion, makes localized explanatory revisions in Sections 2 and 4, and polishes terminology and grammar. The main section sequence remains intact; the remaining appendices are relabeled after the portfolio appendix's removal.

P2.justification: The simulation presentation is substantially reorganized from two consolidated tables into six separately captioned tables grouped by dependence or model complexity. V1 Figure 1 and coefficient Table 5 are removed, while retained figures and appendix tables are redistributed and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the intended interpretation of the detector's parameters and provides more focused exposition and separately organized simulation tables. However, it removes the portfolio illustration and independently fitted stock-market models with uncertainty estimates, reducing support for downstream analysis. With the principal method and detection results unchanged, these clarity gains and losses of applied evidence do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or decline.
